searches.note: Twenty eight searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's. Fourteen were restricted to a house's or a body's own domain (fx-pichler.at twice, vinea-wachau.at six times, bruendlmayer.at twice, gobelsburg.at twice, austrianwine.com twice) and are read as primary through their summaries; four kept the house's own domain out so that the second source would be independent (F.X. Pichler once, Bründlmayer once, Gobelsburg twice); ten went to the open web. The four shared searches are the Vinea Wachau's codex, the Wachau and Kamptal DACs, the Traditionsweingüter, and the Ried rule of 2016 with the legal frame for classified sites of 2023. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the bodies (the Vinea Wachau's codex and vineyard sheets, Austrian Wine, the Kamptal DAC ordinance) for the rules and the sites, then to the houses' own pages for their own dates and methods, then to the open web with the house's domain kept out for the second source of each date and person.

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail was found in no source of this check and rested on one of the author's secondary sources or on no source named, it was cut or said with less (the entrance to Spitz, partly terraced, a release later than most, the fertiliser of 1979, the join of 1784, on its lees at Gobelsburg, the Manhartsberg casks of the Tradition line).

Facts of a house's own history told on its own pages stand, hedged as the house's account; no person is named in prose, as none of the dead met here has dates in two sources (the grower of 1948 has his in the Vinea Wachau's notice alone).

Sources whose title or address names a living person, or a writer's own site, were met among the results but are cited neither in the fragment nor here; the fragment's sources were left as the author wrote them, and the sources of this check are listed per change and per record under extraSources.

tested: The forebear from Rohrendorf in the middle of the nineteenth century and the grandson's purchase at Oberloiben: the house's family page gives the move from Rohrendorf in the mid nineteenth century and the grandson's purchase of a property at Oberloiben in 1898; its timeline gives the winery founded at Oberloiben 27 in 1905. Confirmed; the story now gives both years as the house's.

The F.X. of the name at the wine school of Krems: the house's family page says he graduated from the Krems viticulture college and worked internships in Germany and Alsace. Confirmed; bought prized terraces early on was found in no source and is cut. The German Wikipedia gives him taking over a small holding in 1971, in one source only, so the year is not used.
The Kellerberg of 1990 as the wine that carried the name abroad: the house's timeline, and one secondary portrait. Kept as the house's account.
The new winery of 2009: the house's timeline (Oberloiben 57) and the German Wikipedia, which has the wines made in the new cellar from the 2009 vintage. Confirmed.

The Kellerberg: the Vinea Wachau's sheet gives Gföhl gneiss, the slope sheltered from the westerly winds of the Ice Ages so that loess survives in patches, terraced, facing south to south east, and the name from the Kellerschlössl of Dürnstein, recent, from 1787, a collective name for several smaller vineyards; the house's page gives the same. Confirmed, with the aspect widened and the year added.
Smaragd: the Vinea Wachau's codex and styles page give at least twelve and a half per cent, no enrichment, concentration or aromatisation, and no perceptible wood. Confirmed.
Wachau DAC from the 2020 vintage, hand picking at every level, Riedenwein only Grüner Veltliner and Riesling, never enriched: Austrian Wine. Confirmed.
The word Ried before a vineyard name, required by the amendment of the wine law in force from 14 June 2016: Austrian Wine. Confirmed, so the older label form Dürnsteiner Kellerberg stands.
Unendlich: the house's page gives a Riesling first made in 1998 and a Grüner Veltliner in 2003, and the name from an opera chronicle. Confirmed and dated.
Fully dry: no source gave the Kellerberg's sugar; a Smaragd need only be dry, so the making and the table say dry.
The questions: one key each, four styles and four years; sound.
The rules: nobody living named (the F.X. and his son are described); no price, no score, nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: The grower of 1948: the Vinea Wachau's notice on his death (1923 to 2007) gives the taking over of his parents' holding and his marriage in 1948, his years as mayor of Spitz and his place among the founders and board of the Vinea Wachau in 1983. Confirmed; he stays described, as his dates rest on that one notice.
The first bottling and the single vineyards: the Vinea Wachau's profile of the house credits them to the eldest Franz without a year. Kept as the Vinea's account.

The son who took over in 1983 and led the association from 1988 to 2012: the Vinea Wachau's list of its chairmen (the first from 1983 to 1988, then Franz Hirtzberger from 1988 to 2012, then his successor) and its press text of 2012 on twenty four years in the chair; a sommelier portal and the Vinea's profile give 1983 for the son's start. Confirmed.

The Singerriedel: the Vinea Wachau's sheet gives paragneiss with mica schist and bands of quartzite lower down, shallow, meagre, sandy soil, narrow terraces, Riesling on the steep terraces and Grüner Veltliner at the foot, and a first record of 1486. Confirmed; at the entrance to Spitz and at the edge of the village were found in no source and are now at Spitz; the year 1486 is added.

The making: one merchant gives steel fermentation and élevage in casks of three to five thousand litres; another's sheet for a recent vintage gives steel alone. The record now says often, with some vintages in steel.

The Weinhofmeisterei: a press release of the state of Lower Austria of July 2014 gives the opening of the Hofmeisterei at Wösendorf, in a former vineyard house of St Florian, with the youngest son to build a winery there; an Italian merchant gives the estate's start in 2014; the Vinea Wachau lists it as a separate house. Confirmed.
Hochrain: the Vinea Wachau gives it as a part of the Axpoint at Spitz; the note says nothing of the site, so it stands.

The questions: one key each, four places and four bodies; the explanation of the second now calls the Traditionsweingüter a separate, private association rather than the Kamptal and Kremstal association, since its members reach into the Traisental, the Wagram, Vienna and Carnuntum.
The rules: the house keeps its name; the grower of 1948 is described; his son and grandsons are living and are not named; no price, no score, nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: The family at Unterloiben since the early nineteenth century: several merchants give 1825, one as the family's ownership and another as its vines at Unterloiben; no house page or wine body found. The story's early nineteenth century stands; founded stays empty.

Bottles from the 1950s, the Saint Urban of 1962 and the Vinothekfüllung of 1988 with a Riesling from 2000: the house's profile on the Vinea Wachau gives all four, in English and German, and a Mövenpick sheet gives the baroque Saint Urban first on a bottle in 1962. Confirmed.

The Schütt: the Vinea Wachau's sheet gives a cone of stream debris at the end of the Menthalgraben, carried between the Höhereck and the Loibenberg, deep weathered gneiss, sandier and stonier than the gneiss terraces, low in fine earth, draining well, and the Dürnstein and Unterloiben boundary running through it. Confirmed; partly terraced was found in no source and is cut; the place is made exact.

The making: two searches found no house sheet; Falstaff's sheet for the Kreutles Grüner Veltliner Smaragd of 2023 gives nine months in a large wooden cask. The large old oak casks with some steel rest on the author's importer and the Sommelier Academy; the record now says raised, not fermented, in them.

Released later than most and slow to open: no source confirmed a late release; Falstaff calls the house's name as a late starter incorrect, while agreeing its wines are very long lived. Cut from the ageing, the table and the story, which now say long lived.
The Pfaffenberg in the Kremstal: a merchant and Falstaff's sheet give it as Kremstal, labelled Kremstal DAC from the 2020 vintage. Confirmed, with the trap.
The questions: one key each, four reasons and four images; the lure is the Federspiel's, the lizard the Smaragd's. Sound.
The rules: the house keeps its name; the heads of the last two generations are living and are not named; no price, no score, nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.

The rock: the house's factsheets give desert sandstone of about 270 million years with volcanic inclusions; the Geologische Bundesanstalt's papers give the Zöbing Formation, with the Heiligenstein member an arkose with layers of conglomerate, of the late Carboniferous to the Permian. The label: the house's sheets print Ried Zöbinger Heiligenstein for older vintages and Ried Heiligenstein from 2022. Confirmed.
Organic: two portraits give organic since 2015 and the house's sheets carry an organic control code. Kept.

The Traditionsweingüter: its members reach into the Traisental, the Wagram, Vienna and Carnuntum, so the story no longer calls it the association of the Kamptal and Kremstal estates; Austrian law framed its own Erste and Grosse Lagen only in 2023, so the 1ÖTW line now says so.
Gobelsburg in 1996: the house's press dossier gives the Bründlmayers' recommendation to the abbot and their help at the start. Confirmed.
The questions: one key each, four methods and four estates. Sound.
The rules: the house keeps its name; the son of 1980 and his wife are living and are not named; no price, no score, nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: 1171: the house's history page gives the monks' first vineyards on the Heiligenstein and the Gaisberg, and the German Wikipedia and a merchant's letter give 1171 for the start of winegrowing. Confirmed as the house's account; founded keeps the library's year, with the author's report on what it marks.

1740: the house's history and the German Wikipedia give the sale on 17 September 1740 by an owner ruined by his building, to the abbey of Zwettl. Confirmed; the seller is not named, as no dates were found.

1784: the house's press dossier gives the two properties brought together at Gobelsburg in 1784; its history page gives the move of the making after a fire at Kammern in 1786. In dispute between the house's own pages, so the year is cut and the story says late in the eighteenth century, after a fire at Kammern; the question's 1784 becomes 2008.

The monks to 1995 and the family of 1996: the house's dossier gives a long lease from January 1996, with the Bründlmayers' recommendation and help; an architectural record of the castle gives the abbey's own running until 1996 and a lease since; Vinum gives the contract for two generations. Confirmed, and the lease is added.
850 years in 2021: the German Wikipedia and a merchant's letter. Confirmed.

The Lamm: the house's page gives the south east side of the Heiligenstein where the hill eases into gentler slopes, loess and loam with material from the hill's volcanic rock and Permian silt. Confirmed; at the foot is now on the south east side.

The making: an importer gives the Lamm of 2022 fermented and aged in oak casks of five and six thousand litres, one of them new; a merchant gives casks of five to six thousand litres of Manhartsberg oak. Confirmed; on its lees was found in no source and is cut.

The Kamptal DAC: Austrian Wine gives the 2008 vintage and Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; the ordinance's text gives applications for the state test number of a Riedenwein from 1 April of the year after the harvest. Confirmed.
The 1ÖTW mark: Austrian Wine gives the legal Erste and Grosse Lage of 2023, so the label line and the question's explanation now give the date.
The questions: one key each, four marks and four years. Sound.
The rules: the family of 1996 and the Bründlmayers are living and are not named; the house keeps its name; no price, no score, nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.
